summary: Pelham fire lookout on Jeremy Hill, 1917 to 1981 per a hiking guide; only footings, posts and a concrete pad remain in the state forest.

facts.design: Boxlike cab with windows on all four sides, on steel stilts with guy wires
facts.status_note: Listed as gone; cement footings, metal posts and barrels remain at the summit

access.note: Summit lies within Jeremy Hill State Forest; accounts warn of no-trespassing signs along the path and a private pond beside the route

visit.trail_note: Park in the cul-de-sac at the very end of Jeremy Hill Road; the route to the summit passes a private pond

events.note: A hiking guide gives 1917 as the start of the tower; no construction record was read
Ernest J. Teer kept the tower and its meteorological station
Vandals broke into the state lookout tower and items of value, including watchman Malcolm Popp's tools, went missing
A hiking guide gives 1981 as the end of the tower's years

corrections.why: Pelham is a town, not a county; the Forest Lookouts page for Jeremy Hill gives the county as Hillsborough County. The Forest Lookouts county list also prints Pelham in its county column.

sources.title: You Are Here: Mine Hill & Jeremy Hill

notes_for_editor: The 1917 start rests only on one hiking guide, and no construction record was read, so the built event is weak. The 1934 height and description come from a Lowell Sun piece reprinted on the Forest Lookouts site; the original was not read. The 1981 end date is also the hiking guide's, and no source gives a removal date. The record's county 'Pelham' is a town name; the correction is in corrections. Access: the Forest Lookouts county list and the hiking sources agree the tower is gone, but a visitor's warning about no-trespassing signs and a private pond means the approach should be checked before any visit is suggested.
